title: Check: NetworkPolicy
description: Five questions on restricting Pod traffic.

questions.prompt: With no NetworkPolicy in a namespace, what traffic is allowed?

options.text: All of it - Pods are non-isolated by default

questions.explanation: Kubernetes is allow-all until a policy selects a Pod. From that moment the Pod is isolated for the directions the policy names.

questions.prompt: Which policy denies all ingress to every Pod in a namespace?

options.text: An empty podSelector with policyTypes: [Ingress] and no ingress rules
A policy with ingress: [] and no podSelector field at all

questions.explanation: `podSelector: {}` selects every Pod; listing Ingress in policyTypes with no rules permits nothing.

questions.prompt: Two policies select the same Pod, one allowing port 80 and one allowing port 443. What is permitted?
questions.explanation: There is no deny rule and no ordering. The union of every matching policy is what is allowed.
A cluster whose CNI plugin does not implement NetworkPolicy will accept the object and enforce nothing - a dangerous silent no-op.

questions.prompt: You apply a default-deny egress policy and applications break immediately. What did you forget?

options.text: To allow egress to CoreDNS on port 53

questions.explanation: Name resolution is egress traffic too. Denying it breaks everything before a single connection is attempted.
